text: Triage protocol TRIAGE-001: chest pain presentation. ESI 1-2. Obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Draw troponin, CBC, BMP. Establish IV access. Aspirin 325mg if no contraindication. Activate cath lab if STEMI criteria met. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-002: stroke presentation. ESI 1. Activate stroke team. CT head without contrast STAT. Determine last known well time. NIH Stroke Scale assessment. tPA eligible if <4.5 hours and no contraindications. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-003: sepsis presentation. ESI 1-2. Draw lactate, blood cultures x2, CBC, BMP, UA. Administer 30mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours. Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour. Reassess volume status. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-004: respiratory distress presentation. ESI 1-2. Apply continuous pulse oximetry. Supplemental O2 to maintain SpO2 >92%. Obtain ABG if severe. Chest X-ray portable. Assess for pneumothorax, PE, CHF, asthma. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-005: anaphylaxis presentation. ESI 1. Epinephrine 0.3mg IM lateral thigh immediately. Remove allergen if possible. Establish IV access. Normal saline bolus. Diphenhydramine 50mg IV. Methylprednisolone 125mg IV. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-006: trauma presentation. ESI 1-2. Primary survey ABCDE. C-spine precautions. Two large-bore IVs. Type and crossmatch. FAST exam. CT pan-scan if mechanism warrants. Activate trauma team if criteria met. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-007: pediatric fever presentation. ESI 3-4 (age dependent). Temperature >38C rectal in <3 months = ESI 2. CBC, blood culture, UA for <90 days. Lumbar puncture if <28 days or ill-appearing. Antipyretics after cultures. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-008: abdominal pain presentation. ESI 2-3. Assess for surgical abdomen (rebound, guarding, rigidity). CBC, BMP, lipase, LFTs, UA. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast if surgical concern. NPO if possible surgical candidate. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-009: psychiatric emergency presentation. ESI 2-3. Ensure patient and staff safety. 1:1 observation. Medical clearance labs (BMP, glucose, tox screen, TSH, UA). Assess suicidality with Columbia Scale. Psychiatry consult. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-010: overdose presentation. ESI 1-2. Identify substance (pill count, toxidrome, collateral history). Activated charcoal if <1 hour and airway protected. Specific antidotes: naloxone (opioid), flumazenil (benzo, caution), NAC (acetaminophen). Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-011: chest pain presentation. ESI 1-2. Obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Draw troponin, CBC, BMP. Establish IV access. Aspirin 325mg if no contraindication. Serial troponin at 0, 3, 6 hours. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-012: stroke presentation. ESI 1. Time is brain. Door-to-CT target <25 minutes. Door-to-needle target <60 minutes for tPA. Consider mechanical thrombectomy for LVO if <24 hours with favorable imaging. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-013: sepsis presentation. ESI 1-2. Sepsis-3 criteria: suspected infection + SOFA score increase >=2. qSOFA bedside screen: RR >=22, altered mentation, SBP <=100. If 2+ criteria, assess for organ dysfunction. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-014: respiratory distress presentation. ESI 1-2. Differentiate upper vs lower airway obstruction. Consider BiPAP for COPD/CHF exacerbation. Intubation if GCS <8, inability to protect airway, or refractory hypoxia. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-015: anaphylaxis presentation. ESI 1. Biphasic reaction risk: observe minimum 4-6 hours post-treatment. Discharge with epinephrine autoinjector prescription and allergist referral. Educate on allergen avoidance. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-016: trauma presentation. ESI 1-2. Massive transfusion protocol if hemodynamically unstable: 1:1:1 ratio of pRBC:FFP:platelets. Permissive hypotension (SBP 80-90) until surgical control. TXA within 3 hours of injury. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-017: pediatric fever presentation. ESI 3-4. For ages 3-36 months with T >39C and no source: consider UTI workup. If well-appearing and vaccinated, outpatient management with close follow-up may be appropriate. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-018: abdominal pain presentation. ESI 2-3. Right upper quadrant: consider cholecystitis (Murphy sign, RUQ US). Right lower quadrant: consider appendicitis (Alvarado score, CT). Epigastric: consider pancreatitis (lipase >3x ULN). Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-019: psychiatric emergency presentation. ESI 2-3. Chemical restraint if needed: haloperidol 5mg IM + lorazepam 2mg IM + diphenhydramine 50mg IM (B52). Physical restraints as last resort per policy. Document Q15min assessments. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-020: overdose presentation. ESI 1-2. Common toxidromes: anticholinergic (tachycardia, mydriasis, dry), cholinergic (SLUDGE), sympathomimetic (tachycardia, HTN, diaphoresis), opioid (miosis, respiratory depression, bradycardia). Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-021: diabetic emergency presentation. ESI 1-2. DKA criteria: glucose >250, pH <7.3, bicarb <18, positive ketones. HHS criteria: glucose >600, osmolality >320, no significant ketosis. Both require aggressive IV fluids and insulin drip. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-022: GI bleeding presentation. ESI 1-2. Upper GI bleed: coffee-ground emesis, melena, hematemesis. Lower GI bleed: hematochezia, maroon stool. Glasgow-Blatchford score for risk stratification. Type and crossmatch, CBC, BMP, coags. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-023: syncope presentation. ESI 2-3. High-risk features: exertional syncope, abnormal ECG, cardiac history, older age, no prodrome. Low-risk: situational, vasovagal with prodrome, young and healthy. Risk stratify with San Francisco Syncope Rule. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-024: allergic reaction presentation. ESI 2-3 (ESI 1 if anaphylaxis). Mild: urticaria, pruritus only. Moderate: angioedema without airway compromise. Severe/anaphylaxis: airway involvement, hypotension, GI symptoms. Epinephrine threshold: 2+ organ systems. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-025: headache presentation. ESI 2-3. Red flags: thunderclap onset, worst headache of life, fever with neck stiffness, focal neurologic deficits, altered consciousness, anticoagulated patient. CT head if any red flags. LP if SAH suspected with negative CT. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-026: burns presentation. ESI 1-3 depending on extent and depth. Rule of nines for BSA estimation. Full thickness or >20% BSA = burn center transfer. Parkland formula: 4mL/kg x %BSA crystalloid in first 24h. Airway assessment critical for facial/inhalation burns. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-027: obstetric emergency presentation. ESI 1-2. Precipitous delivery: prepare for neonatal resuscitation. Eclampsia: magnesium sulfate 4-6g IV loading then 1-2g/hr. Placental abruption: emergent C-section if fetal distress. Postpartum hemorrhage: oxytocin, uterine massage, blood products. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-028: eye emergency presentation. ESI 2-3. Chemical exposure: immediate irrigation with 1L NS x 30min before any other assessment. Check pH after irrigation. Acute angle closure glaucoma: timolol, pilocarpine, IV acetazolamide. Central retinal artery occlusion: 90-min window for thrombolysis. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-029: chest pain atypical presentation. ESI 3. Atypical features more common in women, elderly, and diabetics: jaw pain, nausea, fatigue, dyspnea without chest pain. Still obtain ECG and troponin. Consider HEART score for risk stratification and disposition. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-030: back pain red flags presentation. ESI 2-3. Red flags: saddle anesthesia, urinary retention, bilateral lower extremity weakness (cauda equina), fever with IV drug use history (epidural abscess), history of cancer (metastatic compression). Emergent MRI if red flags present. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-031: chest pain presentation. ESI 1-2. STEMI equivalents: new LBBB, de Winter T-waves, Wellens syndrome, posterior MI (ST depression V1-V3 with tall R waves). Posterior leads V7-V9 if suspecting posterior MI. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-032: stroke presentation. ESI 1. NIHSS scoring: 0=no stroke symptoms, 1-4=minor, 5-15=moderate, 16-20=moderate to severe, 21-42=severe. Large vessel occlusion screen: facial droop, arm drift, speech changes. LVO positive = emergent CTA. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-033: sepsis presentation. ESI 1-2. Antibiotic selection by suspected source: UTI=ceftriaxone, pneumonia=ceftriaxone+azithromycin, intra-abdominal=piperacillin-tazobactam, skin/soft tissue=vancomycin, unknown=vancomycin+piperacillin-tazobactam. Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-034: respiratory distress presentation. ESI 1-2. Asthma severity assessment: mild (speaks sentences, SpO2 >92), moderate (speaks phrases, SpO2 90-92), severe (speaks words, SpO2 <90), life-threatening (silent chest, drowsy, SpO2 <90). Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-035: anaphylaxis presentation. ESI 1. Refractory anaphylaxis: repeat epinephrine IM Q5-15min x3 doses. If no response, start epinephrine infusion 0.1 mcg/kg/min. Glucagon 1-5mg IV for patients on beta-blockers. Vasopressin for refractory hypotension. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-036: trauma presentation. ESI 1-2. Pediatric trauma: weight-based dosing for all medications. Broselow tape for equipment sizing. Higher risk of multisystem injury due to smaller body mass. Hypothermia prevention critical. Notify PICU early. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-037: pediatric fever presentation. ESI 3-4. Febrile seizure management: benzodiazepine if >5 minutes. Simple febrile seizure in 6mo-5yo: reassurance, antipyretics. Complex febrile seizure (focal, prolonged, recurrent): workup including EEG consideration. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-038: abdominal pain presentation. ESI 2-3. Elderly abdominal pain: lower threshold for imaging. Atypical presentations common. Consider mesenteric ischemia if out of proportion pain with minimal exam findings. AAA if pulsatile mass or back pain in >50yo. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-039: psychiatric emergency presentation. ESI 2-3. Excited delirium: high mortality risk. Avoid prone positioning. Ketamine 4mg/kg IM for immediate sedation. Aggressive cooling. Continuous cardiac monitoring. Anticipate rhabdomyolysis (aggressive IV fluids, monitor CK). Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-040: overdose presentation. ESI 1-2. Acetaminophen overdose: Rumack-Matthew nomogram for treatment decisions. NAC indicated if 4h level above treatment line or if >150mg/kg ingested and level not yet available. 21-hour IV NAC protocol preferred. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-041: chest pain presentation. ESI 1-2. Right ventricular MI: ST elevation in V4R. Avoid nitrates and diuretics (preload dependent). Aggressive IV fluids. May require dobutamine for RV failure. Consider emergent PCI. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-042: stroke presentation. ESI 1. Intracerebral hemorrhage: reverse anticoagulation immediately (vitamin K + 4F-PCC for warfarin, idarucizumab for dabigatran, andexanet alfa for apixaban/rivaroxaban). SBP target <140. Neurosurgery consult. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-043: sepsis presentation. ESI 1-2. Refractory septic shock: add vasopressin 0.03 units/min if norepinephrine >0.5 mcg/kg/min. Consider stress-dose hydrocortisone 50mg IV Q6H if vasopressor-dependent >6 hours. Central venous access for vasopressors. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-044: respiratory distress presentation. ESI 1-2. Tension pneumothorax: clinical diagnosis - do not wait for imaging. Needle decompression 2nd intercostal space midclavicular line. Followed by chest tube (28-32Fr) in 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-045: cardiac arrest presentation. ESI 1. ACLS algorithm: shockable rhythms (VF/pVT) = defibrillate, epinephrine Q3-5min, amiodarone after 3rd shock. Non-shockable (PEA/asystole) = epinephrine Q3-5min, identify reversible causes (Hs and Ts). Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-046: hypertensive emergency presentation. ESI 1-2. SBP >180 and/or DBP >120 with end-organ damage. Target 25% BP reduction in first hour. IV labetalol, nicardipine, or nitroprusside. Assess for aortic dissection, stroke, ACS, eclampsia. Head CT if neurologic symptoms. Last reviewed: 2026-04-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-047: altered mental status presentation. ESI 1-2. AEIOU-TIPS mnemonic: Alcohol, Epilepsy, Insulin (hypo/hyperglycemia), Opioids/Overdose, Uremia, Trauma, Infection, Psychiatric, Stroke/Seizure. Check glucose immediately. Naloxone if opioid suspected. Last reviewed: 2026-05-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-048: testicular torsion presentation. ESI 2. Time-sensitive: >6 hours = significantly reduced salvage rate. High-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex, acute onset. Doppler ultrasound if available within 30 minutes, otherwise clinical diagnosis and emergent urology consult. Last reviewed: 2026-06-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-049: ectopic pregnancy presentation. ESI 1-2. Consider in any reproductive-age female with abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, or syncope. Quantitative beta-hCG and transvaginal ultrasound. Ruptured ectopic: hemodynamically unstable = emergent OR. Two large-bore IVs, type and crossmatch. Last reviewed: 2026-01-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.

Triage protocol TRIAGE-050: pediatric dehydration presentation. ESI 2-4. Assess degree: mild (<5%, normal vitals), moderate (5-10%, tachycardia, decreased skin turgor), severe (>10%, hypotension, lethargy). Oral rehydration for mild-moderate. IV NS 20mL/kg bolus for severe. Reassess after each bolus. Last reviewed: 2026-02-01 by Clinical Standards Committee.
